he United States Army in Vietnam is a multivolume history of the Army’s involvement in the Vietnam War.

The series treats a full range of topics, from combat operations and advisory efforts to logistics, communications, and engineer endeavors, to relations with the press and activities at the theater command level.
Four combat volumes, of which Staying the Course is chronologically the third, describe the evolution of the Army’s operational strategy and its execution during a long and difficult conflict.
